hints.title: Rewrite the root as a power
hints.body: Convert the square root on the left to a fractional exponent before testing the supplied pairs.
hints.recap: For positive bases, powers of powers multiply exponents.
hints.pitfall: Equal powers do not always force equal exponents when the base is 1.
hints.pause: Find the exponent on each side, then evaluate each supplied pair.

recall.reminder: For positive bases, powers of powers multiply exponents.

hints.title: Check what a counterexample means
hints.body: For each permitted pair, compare the actual two values; record whether it makes the claim fail.
hints.recap: A counterexample obeys every premise but makes the proposed conclusion false.
hints.pitfall: A pair that agrees with the claim is not a counterexample.
hints.pause: Classify the three pairs and select the matching list.

recall.reminder: A counterexample obeys every premise but makes the proposed conclusion false.

solution:
For positive x, xy=xy/2; this is not generally xy.

I: with x=1, both expressions are 1. II: the left side is 24=16, while the right side is 28. Since 8<4, these differ. III: both sides are 32=9.

Only II is a counterexample. Answer C.
knowledgePattern: Test a proposed root/exponent interchange on exact allowed inputs
